sections.title: Getting started
sections.text:
Genesis is a calm game you play in menus. Your character keeps working even when you are away.
- Follow Nixie, the guide. Her first-steps tour shows every system once.
- Stuck? Ask Nixie at the top of How to play. She answers from this guide and the latest patch notes, in your own language. You can ask 30 questions a day.
- Hold the core in the middle of the screen. Everything runs at full speed while it burns.
- Open a zone on the map and take your first fight. Pick a reward and put it on.
- Open the Helper Cache, add the helper to your team and send it on an expedition.
- Learn a profession (the first one costs 1 gold) and take a quest.
- Level up, spend your skill points, and move on to the next region when you are ready.
Where: The tour box with Nixie. Tips can be turned off in Settings. In Settings › Interface you can arrange the Quick access buttons yourself.

sections.title: The core
sections.text:
The core is your engine. Keep it synced and everything earns more.
- Hold the core for a moment to start Core Sync for 30 minutes.
- Without Core Sync the core is dark, and idle work runs at 20 % speed, also crafting queues. A 58 second craft then takes almost 5 minutes.
- While synced: full idle gold, idle XP and +15 % profession output. When it goes dark you earn only a fifth.
- Crits while holding add a minute each.
- Fights, expeditions, quests, work orders and dungeons also add sync time.
- You can bank up to 8 hours of sync. The bar under the core shows how much is left of those 8 hours: more time makes it longer.
- Holding when you have less than 30 minutes left fills it back up to 30 minutes. With more left, holding gives crits that add extra time.
- The core also finds scrap on its own. Better regions give better scrap. Junk comes only from expeditions.
Where: The big hexagon in the middle: "Hold core to assist".

sections.title: Achievements
sections.text:
Goals that pay out gold, credits and permanent bonuses.
- Many groups: fights, gear, helpers, professions, Events, Rifts, Missions, Loyalty and more.
- Forty of them give a permanent idle bonus. Some are hidden — shown as ??? until you earn them.
- Server First: a few titles only one player on the whole server can hold — the first to get there. Once taken, the row shows who took it.
- Travel counts too: trips, time on the road, fuel, skips, drone surveys and how often you return to each region.
- The big ones give Gear Caches, Helper Caches, a Broken Charm or a title. Click a title you have earned to wear it — players see it when they inspect you.
Where: The Achievements button.

sections.title: Auction house
sections.text:
Buy and sell with other players. They often pay more than the vendor.
- Pick an item, the amount and a price.
- Pay a small listing fee up front.
- If it sells you get the gold minus 8 % tax. If not, it comes back to you.
- Filters narrow the list by rarity or by a perk on the gear (Fragment Find, Loot Luck, Player XP…). The coloured frame around a piece shows its rarity.
- Character gems and some materials are Bind on Pickup — the vendor buys them, players cannot.
- Trade directly: tap a player’s name and choose Trade. You each put up to 6 things and some gold in your box — for materials you choose how many to give — then both press Accept. On a computer, press Inventory or Helpers in the trade window and drag things into your column; on a phone, tap Add in the list. Move the window by its title. Helpers can be traded too — take a helper out of your active team first. Any change resets both accepts, so always check the other side before you accept.
Where: The Auction House button, or Trade on a player’s name.

sections.title: Bags & vault
sections.text:
Keep your backpack tidy so new loot fits.
- The backpack has 20 slots to start, and some classes have more. Bags and bag slots add more.
- Search in the toolbar: type a word like "helper" and everything that matches lights up, the rest fades. Esc clears it.
- Bags hold 4 to 14 slots. The bigger the bag, the rarer it is: 8 is Rare, 10 Epic, 12 Legendary and 14 Mythic. Each region has its own bags, and they only drop there.
- To use a bag, tap or click it and choose Equip. It goes into the first free bag slot.
- FULL on the bag button means nothing new fits. Sell, recycle or store things.
- The Vault at The Landing stores extra things. You can look in it from anywhere.
- The Shared tab in the Vault is storage for all characters on your account: 20 slots, unlocked once with 100 credits. Gear, materials, caches and consumables like First Aid Kits and Fuel Cells can go there. The Shared tab opens next to your vault, so you can drag gear both ways between them, and drag things in from your backpack. Moving a stack asks how many, so you can split it. Gold, gems, anything bound and gear with a bound Mod Chip cannot.
- Materials go in the gathering bag, gems in the gem pouch. Shards and marks sit by your gold and take no room.
- Every piece of gear has a grey ★ in its lower right corner. Tap it to give it a star. A starred piece cannot be sold or recycled.
- Tap the star to pick what it is for — Loot Luck, Fragment Find, Dungeon Speed and more. Each has its own colour.
- The filter menu at the top of the Vault shows only one slot (rings, boots, weapons…), one kind of star, one property or one rarity, so you can find a piece fast. It works in the Shared tab too.
Where: The Inventory and Vault buttons.

sections.title: Bugs & ideas
sections.text:
Found a bug or have an idea? Tell us.
- Press Bugs & ideas.
- Say where it happened, what happened and what you expected.
- Send. Ideas are welcome too. The game is in early testing and everything will be reset before release.
- When your report is fixed, or your idea makes it in, you get a letter in your Inbox — with a Gear Cache for a fixed bug, or a Helper Cache for an idea that made it in.
- Letters you have emptied stay in the Inbox for 7 days, then disappear. Unopened letters last 30 days.
Where: The Bugs & ideas button: at the bottom left on a computer, among the menu buttons further down the page on a phone.

sections.title: Charms
sections.text:
Charms let you keep a favourite piece of gear as you level. A charm raises its level, once.
- Beat dungeon bosses and you may find a Broken Charm (Epic, Legendary or Mythic). Never guaranteed, and at most one per run.
- A Jewelcrafter restores it into a whole charm. Both the broken and the whole charm can be sold on the Auction House.
- Use the charm on a piece of gear of the same rarity or lower (a Legendary charm fits Epic gear, never the other way round). The piece gains +10 levels, up to level 60. One charm per piece. Restoring a broken charm costs the Jewelcrafter gold: 200 for Epic, 600 for Legendary, 1,500 for Mythic.
- Only Epic, Legendary and Mythic gear can take a charm. Its health, power and damage grow with the level.
- A level 50 piece becomes level 60 with a charm — the way to push your best gear past the level cap.
Where: Your backpack: tap a charm and pick the piece.

sections.title: Chat, friends & guilds
sections.text:
Everyone plays on the same server. You will see each other as dots on the map.
- Chat in General, Trade (from level 5), Zone, Guild and Whispers.
- A safety check stops hateful, harassing or scam messages before others see them. If yours is stopped, you see it crossed out with the reason, and only you can see that. Whispers are not checked.
- Zone is here and now: only players standing in your zone see it, and nothing is kept — arrive later and you see only what is said from then on.
- Add friends and send them gear you do not need.
- Guilds open at level 10. Weekly operations give caches; permanent guild achievements (dungeons cleared, World Bosses felled, foes by type and more) unlock perks for everyone: a little extra XP and gold, extra boost slots and titles. Only what you do after joining counts.
- Weekly guild operations and guild achievements give guild XP. Every time your guild reaches a new level, everyone in the guild gets a Gear Cache in the mail.
- Hover or tap a player to inspect their gear.
- Click a name and choose Reply, or type @ and a name, to tag someone. They hear a ping.
- Show off gear or a helper: right-click it and choose Link in chat, or Shift+click it while the chat is open. Press C to open or close the chat.
- Link a recipe too: press Link on it in your recipe book, or Shift+click a pattern in your bag. Anyone can hover or tap the link to see what it makes and what it costs.
- Emotes: type /wave, /dance, /cheer, /lol, /bow, /hug, /clap, /ty, /gz, /cry, /facepalm, /flex, /sleep, /shrug or /salute — add a name to aim it (/wave Wolf). /roll rolls 1–100 (or /roll 6). Type /emotes to see the list.
- The 😊 button opens emojis. Your top row holds 10 favourites — press Edit row to choose them. They follow your account.
- Epic, Legendary and Mythic finds are shown in the chat. In the chat settings you choose which finds you see — yours and everyone else’s (Epic is off from the start).
Where: The chat button, Friends and Guild.

sections.title: Crafting
sections.text:
Turn materials into gear and supplies.
- You start with one recipe per slot. Every other recipe is a paper you find and learn.
- Each recipe gives one guaranteed stat. Higher steps add random stats - even the same stat again.
- Hover (or tap) the white ? next to a recipe name to see what it gives: the guaranteed stat, random stats, master chance, item level and rarity.
- Papers drop by region, and each dungeon boss drops papers with its own stats. Heroic gives finer ones. Quests and vendors have papers too.
- Gather the materials and the Crafting Kits: 1, 2, 4, 6 or 8 per step. Costs are the same at every level, and every recipe of a step uses the same materials - only the size of the piece changes the amounts.
- Each step is built on the one below: Journeyman needs tin ingots, Adept iron ingots, Expert platinum ingots, Master voidsteel ingots (and crystals, lenses, cores or plates). Your gathering profession makes those.
- Tap a material you are missing: if one of your professions makes it, you jump straight to that recipe. If not, you see what it is and where it comes from.
- Scrap converts on its own when you craft: 5 of a lower scrap count as 1 of the next, and 1 of a higher scrap counts as 3 of the one below. The recipe shows it in gold: ⇄ uses 1 Phase Scrap. The scrap recipes in Mining never swap.
- Add it to the work order queue. The item gets your level and a random rarity, never below the design’s own rarity - craft again to chase the perfect one.
- Fill queue adds as many as your free queue slots and materials allow, in one tap - even if that is only one.
- Tap a step heading (Novice, Journeyman ...) in the book to fold it away. The game remembers it.
- It is named after what it got, like Lucky Gridwalker Boots of Wisdom. A rare God Roll is extra strong.
- Every recipe has its own look: a Gilded Arc Shield and a Lucky Arc Shield are two different shields. The recipe shows the picture you will get.
Where: A profession card: the book and the work order list.

sections.title: Credits
sections.text:
A rarer currency for shortcuts.
- Credits come from quests, some fights (every elite), expeditions, dungeons, some achievements and daily Transmissions. No daily limit.
- Region vendors trade scrap for 5 credits at a time: 250 Scrap in Voxholm or Sunbreak Junction, 150 Reinforced Scrap in Drakemark or Thimblewild, 100 Charged Scrap in Cutlass Bay or Pearlreach, 50 Phase Scrap in The Last Armada or Sugarwild.
- In The Quarantine, Windfall and Midnight Midway every piece of junk you bring is worth 1 credit.
- Spend them to skip travel or a drone survey: 1 credit per minute left.
- Some Shop items, Mission Board missions, the last bag and vault slots and the Vault’s Shared tab can be paid with credits.
Where: In the left menu, at the top of the screen on a phone.

sections.title: Daily rewards
sections.text:
A free reward every day.
- 30 rewards, one claim per day. Missed days do not reset you.
- Gold, fragments, credits, items and caches. Day 30 is the Genesis Cache.
Where: The Transmissions button.

sections.title: Dungeons
sections.text:
Long runs with bosses that play out in real time, even while you are away.
- Pack supplies: bandages, first aid kits and revive kits.
- Compare your gear score with the dungeon’s required gear score (item level × rarity, averaged over your gear slots), check the forecast, then enter. Your character is busy during the run.
- Come back and claim: gold, credits, fragments, reputation and maybe a schematic. Unused supplies come back.
- Bosses can drop gear of every rarity, all the way to Legendary and Mythic. Heroic never drops Common. Loot Luck helps both how often and how good.
- Heroic opens after you clear the normal one. It has a 2 hour cooldown that starts when the run ends.
- Dungeon Speed on your gear makes every dungeon and Rift shorter. It adds up across your gear, but stops at 25 % shorter in normal dungeons and 50 % in Heroic and Rift — more than that does nothing.
- Rift (level 50, after clearing that dungeon on Heroic): every dungeon has its own Rift, and you climb each one separately. Each level costs 5 Phase Scrap (Rift 25: 125). Pick a level — each one makes the bosses 10 % tougher and 7 % harder hitting on top of Heroic, and gives better gear than Heroic: Rift bosses never drop Common or Uncommon, and higher levels make Legendary and Mythic more likely: about 2 % Mythic per piece in Rift 1 and 10 % in Rift 25 with no Loot Luck — more with it. The dungeon’s signature pieces roll like any other piece, but are never below Rare. XP stops growing above Rift 5. Clear a level to unlock the next. First clear of a new level gives bonus gold, and every fifth level (5, 10, 15, 20, 25) also a Broken Charm. Shares the Heroic cooldown. Your paragon levels count here: each one adds +1 % health and attack inside a Rift.
Where: The Dungeons button, or the last zone of a region.

sections.title: Expeditions
sections.text:
Send helpers away on timed trips for XP, gold, scrap and fragments.
- Be in the region of the expedition you want, with its zone charted, and start it from the Expeditions window.
- Pick a helper and start it. You have one slot per helper in your team.
- Wait: from 5 minutes to 8 hours. Longer trips give more. Starting one adds Core Sync.
- Claim the rewards: XP, gold, scrap and fragments.
- Changed your mind? Abort calls the team home at once, but gives nothing and takes back the Core Sync it gave.
- The first time you finish each expedition it leaves a shard — only once per expedition, never on repeats. Six expeditions in a region = six shards = one gem (see Gems & shards).
Where: The Expeditions button, or a zone on the map.

sections.title: Fights
sections.text:
Every zone has foes. Beat them for XP, money, scrap, fragments and gear.
- Open a zone on the map to see its foes: level, health, attack and how hard it is (Easy to Impossible).
- Press Begin encounter. The fight plays out on its own.
- Win to get XP, money, scrap, fragments and sometimes gear.
- XP follows the foe’s level: foes far below you give almost nothing, foes above you give more.
- A beaten spot gets a new foe after a short rest: 15 s, or 90 s if you still have another foe waiting.
- Elites have three times the health and attack, and give three times the rewards.
- Give up removes a foe, but that spot rests three times longer.
Where: The map: press a zone, then an encounter.

sections.title: Fragments
sections.text:
Fragments are what you spend on caches.
- Fragments drop from fights, expeditions, quests and dungeons.
- Recycle gear you do not need to get more.
- 25 fragments buy a Helper Cache or a Gear Cache. Open one straight away, or buy several to your backpack — both in the Fragments window.
- Opened several at once? The list has Take on each card for the pieces you keep, and Take all, Sell all or Recycle all at the bottom. Sell and Recycle skip what you took and ask first.
- Flip the arrows on either cache for a Rare version (75 fragments, always Rare or Epic) or a Legendary version (250 fragments, always Legendary or Mythic) - for gear and for helpers. The better of the two gets likelier with your Loot Luck and helpers - the card shows your chance. Rare caches open at level 25 or higher, Legendary caches only at level 50; the normal ones open at any level. All three can be bought to your backpack and sent to your own characters.
- Caches follow your level, not the region you stand in: the higher your level, the better the odds of rare results, and a Gear Cache gives gear at your level. Open them anywhere. You can also send caches to your own other characters (Send to alt) - they roll for that character’s level. Loot Luck and your helpers help too: Cache Instinct counts for both caches, Prospector (rarer gear) also counts for Gear Caches and for gear you craft. Loot Luck keeps helping past 100%, just more gently - every extra piece still counts. In fights, dungeons and expeditions it also raises the chance of a gear drop (at half strength; fights stop at 60%).
Where: In the left menu, at the top of the screen on a phone. Press it to open the Fragments window.

sections.title: Fuel
sections.text:
Fuel is what you spend to travel between regions.
- Your tank holds 100 fuel and refills on its own.
- Moving between zones in the same region is free.
- Travel to another region costs fuel and takes time.
- Fuel cells refill the tank. Get them from the Shop, the auction house or a Refiner.
- Right-click a stack of Fuel Cells and pick Merge 10 into Genesis Fuel Cell: ten small cells become one that fills the whole tank. One merge per click.
Where: In the left menu, at the top of the screen on a phone.

sections.title: Gear
sections.text:
Gear gives you Health, Power and Damage, plus extra stats.
- 13 slots: head, neck, chest, legs, feet, gloves, waist, two rings, relic, weapon, off hand and transport.
- Rarity: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic.
- Each piece needs a level to wear. Drag it onto your character, or click it and choose Equip.
- Reroll opens at level 25: change one stat on a piece for gold. No limit — but every try on the same piece costs more than the last, so your purse decides when to stop.
- Reroll never gives a God Roll — those only happen when a piece is made or found. A God Roll stat cannot be rerolled.
- Recycle gear you do not need for fragments, or sell it for gold.
- Wear 3 or more pieces of the same set (head, chest, legs, gloves, boots) and your character shows the full set look. Appearances count too. Crafted sets count by recipe, so 3 Arcweave pieces with the same property make a set.
- Mark gear you love as a ★ Favorite (right-click or the card): it shows a star and cannot be sold or recycled until you remove it. Trading, mailing and the auction house still work.
- Transport gear makes travel faster.
- Save up to 15 gear loadouts and swap between them.
- Old workshop models - Prototype, Surplus, Veteran and more - drop like any other loot, in every slot and rarity.
- Appearance: right-click a piece (or open its card) and pick the look of any piece you have ever owned for that slot. Only the picture changes.
- Two-handed or main hand + off hand? About the same attack either way. A two-handed weapon gets its stats and health ×1.5, but it is only one item. Main hand and off hand get their damage ×1.5 and give you two items’ stats and health.
- Compare: hold Shift over a piece to see it next to what you wear — both rings for a ring, main hand + off hand for a two-handed weapon.
Where: Your character panel and the Inventory.

sections.title: Gems & shards
sections.text:
Each region has a gem with a unique power. You build it from six shards — one from each of the region’s expeditions.
- Every expedition gives one shard — the first time you finish it. Running the same expedition again gives XP, gold and fragments as usual, but no new shard.
- A region has six expeditions (one per zone), so there are exactly six shards to find in each region. The shard icon by your gold shows which ones you have.
- Got all six from the same region? Open the shard icon by your gold and press Forge gem. You can also forge from the gem slot above your character.
- Rolled a weak bonus? Forging frees the shards: run the region’s six expeditions again, get the six shards again and forge a new gem.
- Each shard drops only once, so it can’t be sold or traded — keep it until you have all of them.
- Set the gem in the gem slot above your character. Click the slot to see every gem you own and swap with one tap — pick the gem that fits what you are doing today.
- Powers: Voxholm an extra expedition slot, Drakemark an extra crafting slot, Cutlass Bay free auction listings, Last Armada 25 % off caches, Quarantine a fourth quest, Windfall 20 % less fuel for travel, Sunbreak Junction 10 % cheaper vendor prices, Thimblewild helpers in your team give 10 % more, Pearlreach expeditions 10 % sooner, Sugarwild encounter cooldown 20 % shorter, Midnight Midway a 10 % chance of double gold, XP and fragments from a won fight. Each gem also rolls a bonus percent (on Windfall: more scrap from your core and from dungeons) (on Sunbreak Junction: items sell for more) (on Thimblewild: reputation gained) (on Pearlreach: gold found) (on Sugarwild: profession XP) (on Midnight Midway: reputation gained).
- Reroll a gem (right-click it, or the gem slot): costs 100 gold and a second gem of the same kind from your bag. You see the new rolls first — a new percent on the same ability, or one of two new abilities — and pick one, or keep what you had. Picking a new ability locks the gem to it: later rerolls only change the percent. Percent rolls 15–25 %, a god roll is 30 % (5 % chance). Recycle Fragments on the Drakemark gem stops at 12 %.
- The two new abilities per gem: Voxholm expedition rewards / offline earnings, Drakemark crafting costs / recycle fragments (6-15%), Cutlass Bay dungeon cooldown / elite foe chance, Last Armada World Boss damage / Broken Charm chance, Quarantine healing item power / quest refresh time, Windfall travel time / fuel refill, Sunbreak Junction vendor restock / drone costs, Thimblewild gathering speed / vendor prices, Pearlreach fuel cost / cache price, Sugarwild Sweet Deal (smaller auction house cut) / Treat Bag (dungeon bosses drop gear more often), Midnight Midway Lucky Ticket (half the percent as a chance of an extra piece of gear from a gear cache) / Front Row (more gold and XP from World Bosses).
Where: Any shard in your backpack, or the gem slot above your character.

sections.title: Gold
sections.text:
The main money: 100 copper is 1 silver, 100 silver is 1 gold.
- Shown as 12g 34s 5c: gold, silver and copper.
- You earn it idle, from fights, expeditions, quests, selling and the auction house.
- You spend it on professions, drones, rerolls, bag slots, the Shop and more.
- On a computer, hover your gold to see the exact amount.
Where: In the left menu, at the top of the screen on a phone.

sections.title: Health & rest
sections.text:
Fights cost health. Rest for free, or heal at once with bandages.
- Your health bar sits under your character. It refills slowly on its own, even offline.
- Press Rest to heal to full: 30 s at level 1-10, 1 min at 11-20, 2 min at 21-30, 3 min at 31-40, 4 min at 41-50. You cannot fight while resting.
- Stop ends the rest early and keeps what you healed so far.
- Bandage heals 20 % in 1 second. First Aid Kit heals 50 % in 2 seconds.
- The green cross next to your off hand opens a bar with everything you can use: healing first, then potions, fuel cells last. Click one to use it.
- Revive Kits are packed for dungeons and bring you back at 50 %.
- Bandages come from the Shop, the auction house, or a Medic.
Where: The Rest button above your health bar. The green cross next to your off hand. Bandages are in your inventory.

sections.title: Helpers
sections.text:
Helpers boost you and run your expeditions.
- Get them from Helper Caches: fights, daily Transmissions, or 25 fragments.
- Each helper has its own abilities: more scrap, more XP, faster expeditions and more.
- Only helpers in your team work. Team slots open at level 1, 7 and 12.
- Helpers level up to 25 and get stronger. Rarity (Common to Mythic) never changes.
- When you find a helper you can Take it or Recycle it for fragments right away.
- Helper abilities like rarer gear and cache odds stack on top of your Loot Luck, so they always count, even when your luck is high. Rarer gear works on all gear: fights, expeditions, dungeons, quests, Gear Caches, crafting and the World Boss.
- Helpers in your team learn from everything you do. They grow at the same pace at every level: about a day of normal play takes a new helper to 25.
- At level 25 a helper learns a second ability: a different one, at half strength.
- Shiny helpers are rare and count double on the leaderboard.
- Search your helpers by name, ability or the word shiny, and sort them by level, rarity, ability or Shiny.
- At Halloween five extra helpers can be found: Jacko from The Headless Horseman, Fang and Howl in the event shop, Boo from Helper Caches opened in Voxholm and Bones from Helper Caches opened in Cutlass Bay. They count for your helper achievements.
- Helpers have their own achievements: find new kinds, raise them, build a strong team, recycle and trade - some give a title.
- Save up to 8 helper loadouts to swap your team quickly.
- Mark a helper as a ★ Favorite (right-click): it shows a star and cannot be recycled, not even by Select all.
Where: The Helpers button.

sections.title: Leaderboard
sections.text:
See how you stack up against everyone else.
- Lists: Level, Gold, Fights, Elites, Expeditions, Dungeons, Gear, Helpers, Rift, Achievements and World Boss.
- All time, or This week since Monday. Pick a class to see only that class.
- Level ranks by total XP. Gold is gold earned this week. Rift is your Rift Score: your best Rift level in every dungeon, added together.
- Every Sunday the weekly top list is posted on Discord.
Where: The Leaderboard button.

sections.title: Mail
sections.text:
Letters, rewards and gifts from other players.
- Things that did not fit in your backpack come by mail.
- Take all takes every attachment that fits.
- The × on a letter deletes it right away. A letter that still holds items asks first, so nothing is lost by mistake.
- The Send tab writes a letter: type the character’s name (a list helps you pick), a subject and a message. Attach items opens your backpack — click things to attach them, or drag them into the letter. Stacks ask how many. Add gold, silver and copper under Attached money. Everything goes in one letter. Bind on Pickup things cannot be sent, and caches only to your own characters.
- A letter can also be just words - no gold or item needed. Letters from other players have a Reply button.
Where: The Mail button. Inbox shows what you got, Send writes a letter.

sections.title: Mission Board
sections.text:
From level 50, every Landing has a Mission Board. Each mission costs 25 credits. Do it in that region and hand it in at the same board.
- Each region has its own board with up to 3 missions a day. A new board comes at midnight, Swedish time.
- Missions are drawn from a long list: foes and elites, gathering, quests, expeditions, crafting, recycling, opening caches, buying from the Vendor, the dungeon, Heroic, Rifts and World Bosses. Some only show up if you can do them, like crafting if you have a profession that crafts. Everything you craft counts, in every profession.
- You have 24 hours to finish a mission once you buy it. Hand it in at The Landing in the region it came from.
- Rewards are Gear Caches, Helper Caches and a Gear Focus.
- A Gear Focus lasts 2.5 hours: gear you find and gear from Gear Caches leans toward one property, so that property shows up more often. The Focus guide button on the board explains it and lists them all.
- Different regions offer different properties, so you travel to the region that has the one you want. The board lists them all.
- You can only have one Gear Focus. A new one replaces the old one.
- Some regions give a Region Crate instead of a Gear Focus. Open it from your backpack: one piece from that region’s two gear sets, always Epic or better, at your level. It needs one free backpack slot and cannot be sold or traded.
- It does not take a flask slot, and it does not change gear you craft or buy.
- Missions have their own achievements: how many you hand in, in each region, of each kind, boards cleared and days in a row. Some give a title.
Where: The Landing: open the zone and press Mission Board.

sections.title: Offline progress
sections.text:
Genesis keeps going while you are away.
- Idle gold, XP, professions and expeditions keep running.
- Offline you earn at a lower rate, up to 8 hours. Skills and gear raise both.
- If you switch to another tab or app, you still count as playing for 15 minutes. After that you earn at the offline rate until you come back. A tab you keep on screen counts as playing for up to 12 hours after your last click.
- When you come back, a Welcome back report shows what you earned.
Where: Just log in again.

sections.title: Professions
sections.text:
Professions gather materials and craft things, and they work all the time.
- You can have 2 main and 1 secondary profession.
- Gathering: Mining and Synthetics. Crafting: Outfitter, Weaponsmith, Jewelcrafter.
- Unlearning is free, but you lose that profession's level and recipes. Filling a slot you have used before costs more than a fresh slot; the window shows the price.
- Secondary: Medic (bandages) and Refiner (fuel cells).
- A secondary profession fills its own station (the Medical Bay or the Fuel Refinery). When that station’s storage is full it pauses — your bag has nothing to do with it. Use what is stored, or grow it with Bigger Stores in the skill tree.
- Medic never spends scrap on its own: materials are taken when you place a work order, not while it is being made. Need the scrap elsewhere? Queue no new Medic orders, or Cancel a running one and the unused part comes back.
- Your first profession costs 1 gold. Professions level up to 20. At level 20 the card says MAX LEVEL and crafting gives no more profession XP.
- Recipes with a coloured tag (for example Always Crit Damage) always give that perk, plus the random ones listed next to it.
- Gathered materials go in the gathering bag. It has one slot for every kind your gathering professions can find (at least 10), so everything you gather fits. Materials bought from other professions go in your backpack.
- Ore veins and fiber stashes: open a zone on the map and look for small lime-green dots. Mining sees veins, Synthetics sees stashes. Tap one and stay in the zone for 10 seconds (the cross on the bar or Esc cancels): you get 8–12 of one ore or fiber, and sometimes a gem or a rare material too. What you get follows your profession level, like normal gathering.
- Veins are shared: everyone with the same profession sees the same ones, and the first player to start mining gets it. They pop up at random and fade after an hour if nobody takes them, so keep an eye on the map. Higher regions give better ores more often. You can take 20 a day per profession (new ones at midnight, Swedish time).
- Hover (or tap) a material under Possible finds to see where it drops and how often. Ores and crystals follow your profession level, gems follow the region.
- Refining is instant: Mining turns ore into ingots and crystals into lenses and cores, Synthetics turns fiber into spools, cord and plates. Missing the ingots an ingot needs? Pick how many you want and press Craft — the missing ingots are made on the way, only as many as needed.
Where: The profession cards on the main screen: on the right on a computer, further down the page on a phone.

sections.title: Quests
sections.text:
Quests from the quest givers in the zones.
- Find a quest giver in a zone and accept. Gear rewards are given right away.
- Do the goal. You can have 3 active quests at once - claim finished ones to make room. Expedition, recycle and deliver goals only count in the zone the quest names. Craft goals count only gear from Outfitter, Weaponsmith or Jewelcrafter - not cells, bandages or ingots.
- Claim the rewards. Handing in adds 5 minutes of Core Sync, and sometimes a crafting paper.
Where: The Quests button, or a quest giver in a zone.

sections.title: Regions & travel
sections.text:
Eleven regions. They open in order: Voxholm 1-10, Drakemark 11-20, Cutlass Bay 21-30, The Last Armada 31-40, The Quarantine 41-50, then Windfall, an extra region for level 50. There are also optional side regions with their own gear, and you never need them to move on: Sunbreak Junction, level 5-10, next to Voxholm; Thimblewild, level 15-20, next to Drakemark; Pearlreach, level 25-30, next to Cutlass Bay; Sugarwild, level 35-40, next to The Last Armada; Midnight Midway, level 45-50, next to The Quarantine.
- Reach the region's level: 11, 21, 31, 41 or 50 (Windfall). Sunbreak Junction opens at 5, next door to Voxholm. Thimblewild opens at 15, next door to Drakemark. Pearlreach opens at 25, next door to Cutlass Bay. Sugarwild opens at 35, next door to The Last Armada. Midnight Midway opens at 45, next door to The Quarantine. You must have visited the region before it. A side region only needs the region next door.
- Zoom out on the map and send research drones to survey the region.
- Travel there. It costs fuel and takes a while. The core keeps working while you fly.
- New regions give much more XP when your level matches them.
- Time in a region gives reputation: 1 rep a minute. Fights, dungeons, expeditions and quests there give more. The stars come at 60, 360, 1,440, 4,320 and 10,080 rep. Each star makes that region's vendor 3% cheaper. From four stars the vendor mails you gear at your level once a week (Epic or Legendary); at five it is Mythic.
- In Settings › Gameplay you choose what happens when you arrive in a zone: zoom into the zone, stay on the region map, or open the zone window.
Where: Zoom out on the map to see the world.

sections.title: Scrap
sections.text:
Scrap is what almost every recipe is built from. There are four kinds, from low to high.
- The four kinds: Scrap, Reinforced Scrap, Charged Scrap and Phase Scrap. Higher crafting steps use higher scrap.
- Your core finds scrap while you idle. The kind follows the region: Voxholm and Sunbreak Junction mostly Scrap, Drakemark and Thimblewild Reinforced, Cutlass Bay and Pearlreach Charged, and every region after that Phase. At level 50 you mostly find Phase Scrap everywhere.
- Fights, expeditions, dungeons and gathering also give scrap.
- When you craft, missing scrap is swapped on its own: 5 of a lower kind count as 1 of the next, and 1 of a higher kind counts as 3 of the one below. Mining also has recipes to swap scrap by hand.
- Scrap also pays for ore swaps at the vendor (the Exchange tab): 1 scrap per 2 ore, Phase Scrap first, then Scrap.
- Vendors buy scrap for a few silver if you have too much.
Where: Your backpack and the material shelf. The Exchange tab is at every region vendor.

sections.title: Seasonal events
sections.text:
A few times a year the grid dresses up. For a limited time, fights, expeditions, dungeons and World Bosses drop event marks you spend in the event shop.
- While an event runs, an event button with the event’s mark appears in the menu, and the Events window shows it with a countdown.
- Event marks drop from won fights, from expeditions (longer ones give more), from cleared dungeons and from a slain World Boss (in the letter). They are yours alone: never sold, traded or auctioned.
- The event shop sells an appearance set in five pieces (head, chest, legs, gloves, boots). Buy a piece once and it is unlocked as a look for that slot — it fits any class and any piece of gear.
- Pick the look from a piece’s card: Appearance. Wear all five as your look and your character picture becomes the set.
- The shop also sells a Legendary Cache and a Rare Cache (one of each per day) and boosts for fewer marks.
- At Halloween, The Haunted House opens in The Deepshaft (Voxholm) - pick it at the top of the dungeon window. Normal and Heroic, no Rifts. Its final boss, The Lady in White, has a 10 % chance (20 % on Heroic) to drop a Ghost Sheet: a real chest piece. Wear it, or use it as your chest's look, and you become a little sheet ghost.
- When the countdown hits zero the shop closes. Marks you did not spend stay in your backpack until the same event returns.
Where: The event button in the menu (only while an event runs), or the Events window.

sections.title: Skill tree
sections.text:
Every level gives a skill point. Spend them to shape your character.
- Tap or click a skill to place a point. Take back one (or right-click) removes it. Save when you are happy.
- A red number on the Skill Tree or Paragon tab means you have points left to spend.
- Reset tree gives every point back. It costs 10 gold the first time, then 10 more for every reset of that tree, up to 150 gold. Each tree counts on its own.
- Each profession has its own tree too.
- The last row needs level 50. After 50, Paragon points keep you growing (up to paragon 350, each level costs a little more than the last) — spend them in the Paragon tab, they work everywhere. You can put them anywhere you like, even all of them in one card. Each paragon level also gives +1 % health and attack, but only inside a Rift.
Where: Character panel, the Skills tab.

sections.title: Sockets & Mod Chips
sections.text:
Some gear has a socket. Put a Mod Chip in it for a bonus that stacks with the rest of your gear.
- Some gear drops with a socket. A Socket Press from the World Boss shop (15 Boss Marks) adds one to Rare gear or better. Pressed gear binds to you.
- Jewelcrafters make Mod Chips, and simple Salvaged ones drop in the world. Any chip fits any socket, whatever the rarity of the chip or the piece.
- Each chip type has a cap: Crit Chance 18 %, Crit Damage 25 %, Gold Find 40 %, Dungeon Speed 12 %, Loot Luck 20 %. Mix types to get the most out of your sockets.
- Drag a chip onto a piece with an empty socket to put it in - the game asks first. You can also click the chip and pick the piece from a list. Drag a Chip Extractor onto a piece with a chip to take the chip out.
- Putting a chip in is free. Taking it out needs a Chip Extractor, made by Weaponsmiths. The extractor is used up, the chip is never lost.
- A chip comes back out the way it went in: a chip you could trade can still be traded, a bound chip stays bound. Crafted chips can be traded; Salvaged and fused chips are bound to you.
- Recycling a piece with a chip in it gives you the chip back for free. Selling it sells the chip too. A piece with a chip in it cannot be traded or auctioned.
- Chip Fusion at any vendor: three Salvaged Mod Chips become one Epic chip of a type among the three, for 250g. Anyone can do it.
- Epic, Legendary and Mythic chip recipes are found as Mod Chip Designs in the world. Anyone can find and sell them; only Jewelcrafters can read them.
Where: A small square in the top-left corner of a piece shows its socket (dark = empty). Right-click it, or open its card. Stats shows a Mod Chips row with every type you wear and its cap.

sections.title: The 3D map
sections.text:
The same map as the 2D one, with your character walking around in it. It is new, so it is marked beta, and the 2D map is still there.
- Click or tap the ground to walk. WASD or the arrow keys walk too. Hold Shift to run, press Space to jump.
- Click ! to take a quest and ? to turn one in. Everything else on the map opens the same windows as on the 2D map.
- Zoomed all the way out you see small coloured nodes. Hold the mouse over one to see what it is. Zoom in one step for icons and pillars, and one more for the names.
- Colours: yellow quests, white encounters, blue expeditions, red dungeons, green vendor, purple vault, pink missions. You are orange.
- Zones you have not charted are grey and empty until a drone has surveyed them.
- Pick your own figure in your Profile: 3D character. It only changes how you look in the 3D world. Every figure has three colours that only change the clothes. Skeletons, the Paladin and the third colour are unlocked with achievements.
- The glow and the clock can be changed in Settings: Power and Interface.
- Thanks for the free 3D models: Kay Lousberg (KayKit), Quaternius, Kenney, CreativeTrio and iPoly3D, and under CC-BY 3.0: Alex Safayan, Braden Brunk, CG ART Creation, Cael Hansen, Danni Bittman, Daqian Dong, J-Toastie, Jake Blakeley, Poly by Google, Steve Atkins, Yogoshimo 2.0.
Where: The 2D | 3D switch at the top of the map.

sections.title: World Boss
sections.text:
Every day at 12:00 and 18:00 Swedish time a World Boss lands in one zone. They take turns, so you meet two different bosses each day. Everyone who gets there and fights shares the spoils.
- An hour before, a red bar appears above the map, a skull marks the zone in that region, and the chat says where. Travel to that zone — no drone needed while the boss is around.
- When it lands you have up to 15 minutes to bring it down. Open it from the Events button, the red bar, the skull, or the boss line in chat.
- You have five moves: Quick Strike (every 3 s), Heavy Strike (every 10 s), your Ultimate (triple damage), Dodge and Heal (+40 % health, every 30 s). Each card shows the damage you deal with it. Dodge and Heal unlock after your first strike.
- Quick and Heavy Strikes charge your ultimate meter: +10 % and +25 %. When it is full, the Ultimate lights up.
- The boss also sends out shockwaves you cannot dodge: a small one every 50 s and a big one every 30 s. Watch your health and Heal in time.
- The boss grows with every fighter who joins, based on what a hero of that level is expected to hit. Better gear than that means a faster kill.
- Every 30 s the boss winds up a special attack. The screen warns you — press Dodge in time and it misses. Otherwise it may freeze you, hit you hard or weaken your strikes.
- Knocked out? You get back up after 20 s with half your health. Nothing is lost.
- Your class has its own five moves: same timers for everyone, each with a small twist. A Breaker hits hardest first, a Runner is fastest, a Warden fights with the team, a Fabricator holds out and a Prospector gets more from the fight. The Events window lists yours.
- When the boss lands and you stand in its zone, the fight card opens by itself: the boss, your health and your five buttons. The Events window keeps the rules, the bosses and your Boss Marks.
- Everyone who struck gets the Worldsaver buff: +10% gold and +10% XP for 1 hour — even if the boss escapes. It does not take a potion slot.
- When it falls, everyone who struck gets XP right away and a letter with gold, a piece of gear, and a chance at a signature piece, a schematic or a Broken Charm. Top damage gets a little extra. If it escapes you still get half the gold and XP and a plain piece. Letters are kept for 30 days — open them.
- Every kill also puts a Boss Mark in the letter. Spend them in the Events window: 2 marks = a guaranteed Legendary piece, 10 marks = a guaranteed Mythic piece, and Broken Charms for 5 (Epic), 7 (Legendary) or 10 marks (Mythic).
- During some holiday events an extra World Boss comes every evening, like The Headless Horseman at Halloween (21:00 Swedish time in The Village, Voxholm). It gives the usual letter, a Jacko helper and 10 Jack-o'-Marks, but no signature pieces and no Broken Charms.
- A Battle Report pops up when it is over: your damage, your share of the boss, your rank and the top list. Open it again with the Battle report button.
- Your damage follows your Power, Damage, Health and crit — better gear hits harder, with no cap.
- The numbers tell you what landed: white is a normal hit, gold a crit (the screen gives a small shake) and purple your Ultimate. In the fight log the boss’s own attacks are red.
- Between bosses the Events window is a codex: every boss, its special attacks and what it drops.
Where: The Events button (it glows until you have opened it once), or the skull on the map while a boss is announced.

sections.title: Your stats
sections.text:
Stats from gear, helpers, skills, paragon and your gem add up. The Character panel shows the total and where it comes from.
- Loot Luck — rarer pieces from fights, caches, expeditions and dungeons. No hard cap: up to 100% every point counts fully, above that it keeps helping, just more gently. In fights, dungeons and expeditions it also raises the chance of a gear drop (at half strength; fights stop at 60%).
- Gear Drops — more pieces from fights and dungeon bosses (up to 60% per fight win, 95% on bosses).
- Fragment Find and Gold Find — more fragments and gold from fights, dungeons, expeditions, quests and idle time. Recycling is not affected. Your gem counts too. Cap 100%.
- Player XP — more XP from everything. No cap.
- Crit Chance — the chance that a hit is a critical hit. Everyone starts at 15%, gear and class add more. Stops at 60% in total.
- Gear score — item level × rarity, averaged over your 13 gear slots (an empty slot counts as 0, your gem does not count). A full set of level 50 Mythic gear is 210. Dungeons show a required gear score, and the Gear leaderboard ranks it.
- Crit Damage — how hard a critical hit lands. Everyone starts at ×1.75 (a crit hits 1.75 times as hard), and Crit Damage on gear adds to that: +25% makes it ×2.0. Your Character panel shows your total.
- Armor — less damage taken, up to 60%.
- Dungeon Speed — shorter dungeons, up to 25% (up to 50% in Heroic and Rift).
- Expedition Speed — shorter expeditions, up to 80%. Travel Speed — faster travel, up to 60%.
- Crafting Speed, Gathering Speed and Profession XP — faster profession work and more profession XP. They count toward the same caps as the profession skill tree (40% gathering, 60% crafting); Profession XP stops at 100%.
- God Roll Chance — a chance that a new piece rolls top values, up to 10%.
- Helpers add on top: Cache Instinct (rarer caches), Prospector (rarer gear), Study Partner (XP) and more.
- Tip: the same stat on many pieces adds up — chase the total, not one perfect piece. The Character panel tells you when a stat has hit its cap.
Where: The Character panel (Stats).

sections.title: Zones
sections.text:
Each region has zones with foes, quests and expeditions.
- A zone must be charted by a drone before you can use it.
- Every region has The Landing with the Vendor, the Vault and the Mission Board.
- Moving between zones in a region is free.
- Double-click a charted zone on the map to travel there at once. In Settings › Gameplay you choose if the map then zooms into the zone or stays on the region map.
- The last zone in each region holds the dungeon.
- At level 50 every region is balanced for you: foes, loot, gold, XP, gems and schematics are as good in Voxholm as in The Quarantine. Play wherever you like.
Where: The map: press a zone to open it.
